final_candidates.decision_summary: Helix-breaking Pro at GP1 apex/core residue L107, a documented antigenic surface for class I antibodies like those in the Arevirumab-3 cocktail. Plausible local epitope disruption with modest folding risk, preserving the LAMP1-binding region.

Removal of an aromatic side chain in the exposed GP1 head; aromatic residues frequently dominate antibody-paratope contacts, so alanine substitution is a classic escape mode with low expected impact on entry.
Charge-introducing substitution on a predicted surface-exposed GP1 loop that can repel antibody binding while leaving receptor-binding and entry functions largely intact.

stop_reason.detail: Candidate pool is self-consistent, all WT residues verified, and no external evidence is available to justify further rounds.

history.rationale: GP1 loop residue within the 12.1F/37.2D antigenic surface; substitution to Pro is expected to locally disrupt antibody binding while lying outside the conserved LAMP1 receptor-contact region, preserving entry.

L107 sits in the GP1 N-terminal distal region near known 12.1F/37.2D contact areas; proline may locally disrupt antibody binding with modest folding cost. No new evidence available, so confidence unchanged.

GP1 residues near the GP1 core/apex are documented antigenic surfaces for class I antibodies like those in the Arevirumab-3 cocktail; a helix-breaking Pro at 107 is a plausible local epitope disruption with modest folding risk, so it is promoted to rank 1.
N119 sits in an exposed GP1 epitope loop overlapping the 37.2D footprint; a charge-reversal mutation can weaken neutralization with limited impact on receptor engagement.
Surface-exposed glycosylation-adjacent position; charge reversal can perturb antibody paratope contact while rarely destabilizing the core fold.
A charge-introducing substitution on a predicted surface-exposed GP1 loop can repel antibody binding while leaving the LAMP1-binding/site integrity largely intact.
H124 is adjacent to a known antibody contact region in GP1; mutation to a smaller polar residue can reduce binding affinity of the cocktail components while maintaining fold.
A solvent-exposed His in the antigenic GP1 head; substitution to Asn could introduce a subtle surface change affecting 8.9F/12.1F recognition.
Conservative-ish surface substitution within the same antigenic region; moderate escape potential with low viability cost.
Y150 is a surface-exposed aromatic residue likely contributing to antibody paratope contacts; alanine substitution reduces hydrophobic recognition with modest structural cost.

Y150 lies within the CD-M8 epitope-proximal surface frequently implicated in Arevirumab-3 evasion, so its escape value is arguably higher than initially ranked. Slight caution because Ala removes a large aromatic side chain that could contribute to local stability.
Aromatic side chains frequently dominate antibody-paratope contacts, and Y150 sits within the exposed GP1 head; alanine scanning-style removal is a classic escape mode, retained near the top.
Introducing an N-glycosylation sequon near a GP1 distal-loop epitope could shield antibody access (glycan masking) while leaving the core entry machinery intact.
S255 is near the 8.9F/37.2D footprint around residues 253-263 where substitutions are documented escape routes; raising confidence despite lack of external evidence.
GP1 C-terminal region near the SSP interface may contribute to 8.9F-like contacts; N-linked-glycan-providing mutation could sterically shield the epitope.
L128 lies within an antibody-accessible GP1 loop; proline substitution distorts local backbone conformation recognized by neutralizing antibodies.
Adjacent to epitope residues but Pro in a helix-capable region carries elevated folding risk; retain at low confidence pending further iteration.
Kept as a secondary structural-disruption candidate but lower confidence due to folding risk.
I112 is in a solvent-exposed GP1 region proximal to antibody footprints; a polar substitution can alter epitope surface chemistry without touching conserved receptor-binding residues.
Conservative substitution with limited predicted antigenic impact; keep for diversity but low ranked.
Modest, size-conservative change unlikely to substantially disrupt a paratope; low expected escape payoff.

rejection.reason: Modest, size-conservative change unlikely to substantially disrupt a paratope; low expected escape payoff.

history.rationale: Q149 is surface-exposed and adjacent to epitope residue Y150; adding positive charge can reduce antibody affinity while preserving GP1 fold.
Solvent-exposed charge change; plausible but no strong structural argument.
Charge introduction at 149 is redundant with Y150A at the same epitope region and Y150A is the stronger perturbation.

rejection.reason: Charge introduction at 149 is redundant with Y150A at the same epitope region and Y150A is the stronger perturbation.

history.rationale: K170 is an exposed charged residue in a GP1 loop that may contact 8.9F; charge reversal could weaken binding while remaining outside the LAMP1 interface.
K170E is in a buried/interface region unlikely to contact the cocktail antibodies and charge reversal could impair trimer integrity, reducing viability risk/reward balance.

rejection.reason: K170E is in a buried/interface region unlikely to contact the cocktail antibodies and charge reversal could impair trimer integrity, reducing viability risk/reward balance.

history.rationale: P145 lies in a flexible epitope-proximal loop; substitution increases loop flexibility, potentially reducing antibody avidity while keeping entry function.
P145S is a backbone-conformation-sensitive position; deleting Pro may destabilize a loop needed for GP1 folding without clear escape benefit.

rejection.reason: P145S is a backbone-conformation-sensitive position; deleting Pro may destabilize a loop needed for GP1 folding without clear escape benefit.

history.rationale: Adding a glycosylation-competent Asn adjacent to S255 (with downstream S/T) could create a de novo N-linked glycan shield over a C-terminal GP1 epitope, a well-established arenavirus immune-escape mechanism.
